'''Trevor Evans''' (1925–1991) was a mathematician specializing in [[abstract algebra]], [[finite geometry]], and [[Word problem (mathematics)|the word problem]]. Originally British, he worked for many years in the US.

==Early life and education==
Evans was born on December 22, 1925, in [[Wolverhampton]]. He read mathematics at the [[University of Oxford]], receiving a bachelor's degree in 1946. After a 1948 master's degree from the [[University of Manchester]], he returned to Oxford for a master's degree in 1950 and a doctorate (D.Sc.) in 1960.{{r|obit}} His doctorate was granted based on 12 previous publications rather than on a dissertation; it was jointly advised by [[Graham Higman]] and [[Philip Hall]].{{r|mg}}

==Career and later life==
From 1946 to 1950, Evans was an assistant lecturer at the University of Manchester. He moved to the US in 1950. After becoming an instructor at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] in 1950,{{r|obit}} he took a faculty position at [[Emory University]] in 1951.{{r|emory}} He remained at Emory for the rest of his career, despite several other visiting positions: he joined the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in 1952, and became a research associate at the [[University of Chicago]] in 1953. Later he visited the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln|University of Nebraska]], the [[California Institute of Technology]], and the [[Darmstadt University of Technology]] in Germany.{{r|obit}}

He headed the mathematics department at Emory from 1963 until 1978,{{r|obit}} and was given the Fuller E. Callaway Professorship of Mathematics in 1980.{{r|emory}} His notable students included [[Etta Zuber Falconer]], who completed her doctorate under his supervision in 1969.{{r|mg|emory}}

==Awards==
Emory University gave Evans their 1972 Emory Williams Distinguished Teaching Award for Graduate Education. He was also a recipient of the distinguished service award of the Southeastern Section of the [[Mathematical Association of America]].{{r|emory}}

An undergraduate award, the Trevor Evans Award, is given in memory of Evans by the Emory University Department of Mathematics.{{r|emory}} Another award with the same name, the Trevor Evans Award, is given annually by the [[Mathematical Association of America]] for an outstanding publication in its undergraduate mathematics magazine, ''[[Math Horizons]]''.{{r|maa}}
